scope.objective: Cross-reference target MediaTek and Nothing camera metadata families against revision-pinned public MediaTek, ChromiumOS, AOSP and official Galaga kernel sources.
scope.interpretationRule: Entries are analogues or name/type/flow matches only. No public source is treated as an exact implementation-equivalent definition of the Galaga Android 16 camera stack.

sources.scope: Current indexed repository head used to bound freshness and confirm the continuing public MediaTek HAL tree.
sources.targetRelation: Different product, SoC, operating environment and userspace integration; never an exact Galaga match.

sources.scope: Revision with indexed logical-camera, feature-policy, capture/streaming, sensor, metadata, IPC and MFB/HDR parameter interfaces.
sources.targetRelation: Public architectural analogue from an older SoC and camera middleware generation.

sources.scope: Revision indexing pass1 synchronization and pass2 request API managers.
sources.targetRelation: Request scheduling analogue only; no Android Camera2 vendor-tag equivalence.

sources.scope: Revision indexing capture nodes, streaming nodes, pipeline-session construction and stream configuration policy.
sources.targetRelation: Feature-graph analogue only; target feature nodes, tuning and scheduling may differ.

sources.platform: AOSP Android 16 camera metadata C API
sources.scope: Defines vendor-tag boundaries, enumeration callbacks, section naming and runtime type lookup contracts.
sources.targetRelation: Normative metadata transport contract; it does not define MediaTek or Nothing tag semantics.

sources.scope: Target-specific sensor topology, CSI wiring, ISP subsystem, calibration, PDA, clocks and device configuration.
sources.targetRelation: Official Galaga source, but release 260415-1710 predates observed build 2606151653 and omits proprietary userspace.

matches.finding: AOSP defines how vendor sections, names, tags and native metadata types are enumerated and transported, while leaving vendor-specific semantics outside the public standard.
matches.platformDifference: The target key names and values must be recovered from the Galaga provider/runtime; AOSP supplies no MediaTek or Nothing enum meanings.

matches.finding: The public MediaTek HAL exposes legacy MFB mode names for MFLL, AIS and automatic selection.
matches.platformDifference: These are Camera1-style string parameters from an MT8183-era ChromeOS tree, not the target Camera2 vendor-tag value table.

matches.finding: Public source separates sensor HDR capability/mode enums from higher-level HDR parameters and pipeline policy.
matches.platformDifference: The target advertised multi-stream HDR values, including 6, cannot be assigned these historical enum meanings without target runtime evidence.

matches.finding: The public HAL has explicit logical-device, supported-feature and multi-sensor synchronization abstractions.
matches.platformDifference: Their presence does not prove Galaga exposes auxiliary physical IDs or uses the same logical grouping and feature bits.

matches.finding: Public policy code represents a main capture frame plus subframes and optional pre/post frames, with an explicit ZSL-flow decision.
matches.platformDifference: This does not define target ZSL timestamps, prerelease semantics, postview buffers or frame-count vendor values.

matches.finding: The public stack uses a policy-selected capture feature graph with P2 processing nodes, per-request inference and multi-frame request objects.
matches.platformDifference: Node names and flow shape are architectural analogues; target ISP tuning blobs, feature combinations and vendor keys remain proprietary.

matches.finding: Public code separates streaming feature nodes, session construction and stream-configuration policy.
matches.platformDifference: The Nothing EIS and SOIS keys have no proven one-to-one mapping to these ChromeOS feature nodes.

matches.finding: Public MediaTek code contains separate pass1 synchronization and pass2 request API managers around V4L2 request execution.
matches.platformDifference: The target may use a newer ISP7SP request path and different userspace/kernel APIs.

matches.finding: The public ChromeOS implementation isolates 3A control behind explicit client/server IPC adapters.
matches.platformDifference: ChromeOS uses a sandboxed camera-algorithm IPC model; Galaga Android userspace and daemon boundaries must be observed independently.

matches.finding: Public interfaces expose per-session sensor scenarios, continuous configuration and policy-produced request frame sets that could support mode switches without defining target seamless or in-sensor-zoom keys.
matches.platformDifference: No exact public symbol matches the target key names; this is a structural hypothesis rather than a semantic match.

matches.finding: Official Galaga source proves four wired sensor nodes and MT6878 camera/ISP interfaces below Android userspace.
matches.platformDifference: Kernel topology cannot identify the Android logical-camera policy, public camera IDs, vendor-tag semantics or stock routing decisions.

matches.finding: No exact public MediaTek or AOSP symbol match is recorded for the three Nothing-specific target families.
matches.platformDifference: These keys remain target-only unknowns; similarly named EIS or tuning components must not be used to infer their types or values.

platformDifferences.statement: Most indexed ChromiumOS content is MT8183-era, while Galaga uses MT6878 and the official kernel tree exposes ISP7SP-era components.
platformDifferences.consequence: Class names and flow structure may transfer as hypotheses, but enum values, nodes, metadata layouts and feature support may not.

platformDifferences.statement: Several public matches are legacy Camera1 string parameters, whereas the target inventory is Camera2 characteristic/request/result/session metadata.
platformDifferences.consequence: Name similarity cannot establish native metadata type, direction, valid values or writeability.

platformDifferences.statement: ChromeOS integrates the HAL through Mojo and sandboxed camera-algorithm IPC, while the target runs an Android 16 CameraProvider/CameraService stack.
platformDifferences.consequence: IPC adapters and process boundaries are structural analogues, not target call paths.

platformDifferences.statement: The detailed public MediaTek content revisions predate the 2026 Galaga firmware and may represent older middleware generations.
platformDifferences.consequence: Every target inference requires runtime or build-matched binary confirmation.

platformDifferences.statement: Official Galaga kernel source exposes sensors and ISP interfaces but omits the exact provider, feature graph, vendor-tag table, tuning and stock application.
platformDifferences.consequence: Kernel source cannot close userspace routing or vendor-key research.

platformDifferences.statement: Public logical-camera abstractions and four wired Galaga sensor nodes do not prove third-party access to auxiliary optics.
platformDifferences.consequence: Public IDs, physical metadata, package identity and stock-only routes must remain separately tested.

hypotheses.claim: Target MFB values may select MFNR, AIS or automatic multi-frame policy before capture-graph construction.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Use the typed-key runtime trace and guarded probe harness to compare accepted values against burst frame count, exposure spread, motion sensitivity, result metadata and output latency on public camera ID 0.
expectedObservations: Mode-dependent frame count or capture latency
Consistent request/result value echo or feature-result marker
hypotheses.falsifier: All accepted values produce indistinguishable single-frame requests and no correlated result or timing change across repeated trials.

hypotheses.claim: The target advertised HDR value 6 may select a middleware feature mode rather than directly reuse historical sensor VHDR enum values.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Record stock and guarded-probe requests with synchronized capture results, sensor exposure times, gains, frame count, sensor mode/scenario and output histograms.
expectedObservations: Multiple exposure groups or HDR-specific feature frames
A stable value-to-result or value-to-sensor-scenario correlation
hypotheses.falsifier: Value 6 is rejected, ignored, or consistently produces no metadata, exposure, frame-count or output difference from value 0.

hypotheses.claim: Target ZSL, postview and prerelease keys may govern buffer selection and request-policy branches rather than optical routing.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Trace request creation, image/result timestamps, selected ZSL timestamp, postview stream configuration and background-service request keys during stock still capture.
expectedObservations: ZSL timestamp selects a prior converged frame
Postview or prerelease changes buffer/session behavior without changing physical focal length
hypotheses.falsifier: The keys never appear in stock requests/results and guarded changes do not alter timestamps, buffers, session configuration or latency.

hypotheses.claim: CameraFlex and multicamera metadata may configure a proprietary logical-device policy over the four wired Galaga sensors.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Compare stock 0.6x/1x/2x sessions using key-type traces, CameraService/Binder metadata, logical/physical result IDs, sensor timestamps and package-identity-controlled launches.
expectedObservations: Session-only key changes correlate with physical sensor activation
Logical result or synchronization behavior differs by stock route
hypotheses.falsifier: Stock optical route changes occur with no CameraFlex/multicam metadata, logical/physical metadata, or sensor-activation correlation.

hypotheses.claim: In-sensor zoom and seamless keys may select sensor scenarios or crop/remosaic modes while retaining one logical session.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Trace stock zoom transitions and guarded probes while recording sensor mode IDs, crop regions, active physical sensor, focal length, remosaic metadata, session recreation and frame discontinuities.
expectedObservations: Scenario/crop changes without a full camera reopen
A vendor-key transition precedes or accompanies sensor-mode or physical-route change
hypotheses.falsifier: All optical transitions require full reopen or occur without any target key, sensor-scenario, crop or remosaic correlation.

hypotheses.claim: Target ISP tuning, raw-reprocess and frame-index hints may feed feature-graph/P2 request construction rather than directly control the sensor.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Correlate stock request keys and result blobs with capture graph frame indices, raw/YUV inputs, P2 request timing, output format and ISP metadata sizes.
expectedObservations: Frame-index/tuning-index sequences align with a multi-frame capture
ISP metadata appears on P2/reprocess paths rather than sensor controls
hypotheses.falsifier: The keys map only to sensor controls or show no consistent relation to P2, reprocess, frame indexing or ISP metadata.

hypotheses.claim: Nothing-specific EIS/SOIS metadata likely extends or parameterizes a streaming stabilization path but has no safe public enum mapping.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Capture stock video/preview traces with stabilization toggles and compare key types, request values, crop margins, gyro/EIS metadata, frame latency and session configuration.
expectedObservations: Nothing key changes correlate with stabilization mode or crop/latency
The native type remains stable across routes and builds
hypotheses.falsifier: The keys are absent from stock stabilization flows or changes do not correlate with stabilization, crop, gyro, latency or output motion.

hypotheses.claim: Galaga may retain a separate MediaTek 3A control boundary even though its Android process and transport differ from ChromeOS.
hypotheses.testProtocol: Use build-matched process maps, Binder/IPC traces, library imports and synchronized 3A request/result metadata to identify the first userspace component consuming AE/AWB/AF vendor controls.
expectedObservations: A distinct 3A service/library boundary receives per-frame controls
3A result metadata is emitted after that boundary
hypotheses.falsifier: All 3A logic is in-process with the provider and no separate transport, service or library boundary is observable.

nonClaims: A matching class, parameter or enum name does not prove identical numeric values, native metadata types or runtime effects on Galaga.
The public MT8183-era ChromeOS implementation is not treated as source for the Android 16 MT6878 proprietary HAL.
Four wired sensors in the Galaga device tree do not prove that third-party applications can open four public or physical camera IDs.
The index does not authorize writing unknown vendor keys; guarded probes remain subject to typed-key and safety policies.
The absence of an exact public symbol match does not prove that a target feature is implemented only by Nothing.
This cross-reference does not close the typed vendor-tag database, build-matched firmware, stock-app or target-binary issues.

updateTriggers: A new official Galaga source release or exact 2606151653 source drop appears
The target firmware or stock camera package changes
Runtime traces establish native types, values or effects for an indexed family
A newer public MediaTek implementation exposes a closer MT6878/ISP7SP analogue
